approach: Fix the reported position loss by DELETING SurveyView's mount-time surveySessionStore.reset() — both genuine start-over paths (handleStartOver, WelcomeScreen 'I'm new') already reset explicitly, so the deletion satisfies FR-002/003 and cascades to fix D-2/D-3/D-4 with no new mechanism. Then widen the hash to #route/step/question behind one pure resolver and one jump primitive shared by trail deep links, footer dots and breadcrumb. Make Compare structurally read-only via a new useCompareArtifact that never wires onInstantiate, leaving usePreviewArtifact untouched for Output.

decisions.decision: Fix D-1 by deleting SurveyView mount reset, adding no replacement mechanism
decisions.why: grep finds exactly three surveySessionStore.reset() call sites; the two genuine start-over paths (handleStartOver StudioShell:1073, WelcomeScreen I am new :168) already reset explicitly, so the mount reset is pure defect. Deleting it also fixes D-2 (durable overwrite), D-3 (all four entry points) and D-4 (Phase B alphabet) at once.
decisions.rejected: A hasNavigatedWithinSession flag or a route-aware reset - both add a second notion of session identity beside the two explicit paths, keeping the very framing (component lifetime as session boundary) that is the bug.

decisions.decision: Compare isolation is structural: a new useCompareArtifact that never passes onInstantiate
decisions.why: FR-025 requires the absence of a write path, not a guarded one. Not passing the callback means instantiateFromBaseIfConfirmed is unreachable, so there is no rebase dialog and no phaseResults/irAxes reset. usePreviewArtifact stays untouched for Output per FR-026.
decisions.rejected: A readOnly:true flag on usePreviewArtifact - the guarantee would then rest on the flag being passed at every call site, and a future site that forgets it silently re-arms the two-click session-loss trap.

decisions.decision: Per-tab view state is a module-level zustand singleton with no storage layer
decisions.why: A module singleton survives a route unmount and dies with the JS context - exactly Q9 default (survives tab switches, not reloads) achieved by construction, with zero persistence code. Satisfies FR-051/052/053 and matches the existing three-store house idiom.
decisions.rejected: sessionStorage (survives a reload, violating Q9 and needing explicit start-over clearing) and adding view state to TraversalSnapshot (FR-051 forbids it in v1).

decisions.decision: Widen the hash to #route/step/question; keep RouteId and the preview route token unchanged
decisions.why: Smallest change satisfying FR-010/011 while honouring FR-006 and the retained-hash-router assumption. Step and question ids are reserved-character-free slugs so no escaping is needed. Keeping the preview token avoids breaking every bookmark and e2e hash assertion for no requirement - FR-026 scopes the rename to labels, aria names, ids, tests and docs.
decisions.rejected: Query form #survey?step=... (two grammars in one hash) and a client-side router library (named in the spec Out of scope).

decisions.decision: Keep the history bridge design; re-derive its premise and re-point its DEV ordering guard
decisions.why: Traced against a preserved store the hook gets MORE correct: tab-switch entries carry null state so they no-op as foreign; the mount tag now agrees with the store in both the fresh and preserved cases; expectedBackTarget computed from preserved history matches the pre-departure entries instead of being stale. FR-016 keeps both accepted degrades closed.
decisions.rejected: Rebuilding the bridge on the new Location grammar (couples two changes; ksStep already carries what the prediction needs) and routing in-app Back through history.back() (FR-016 makes that a separate explicit decision, and it would invalidate every synchronous in-app-Back assertion).

decisions.decision: Footer dots derive from effectiveEntries filtered to survey-answer payloads; labels reuse createLookupQuestionLabel
decisions.why: effectiveEntries already collapses supersession chains, so FR-042 one-dot-per-revised-question needs no rule of its own. Q1 default maps onto payload.kind exactly - notice nodes and acknowledgement screens record nothing and are excluded with no filter written. Reusing the trail label helper gives FR-043/044 one localized implementation.
decisions.rejected: A dedicated progress counter in the survey store (second source of truth for which questions are done) and excluding by an *_confirm id pattern (Q1 shows it is wrong - pb_rtl_direction_confirm is a required routing boolean).

decisions.decision: The footer IS the breadcrumb (Q7); no separate breadcrumb bar
decisions.why: Author directive: one narrow strip with navigation dots serves both where-am-I and jump-back. US6 folds into US4; FR-060..063 become footer orientation requirements (current-position marker) rather than a separate bar.
decisions.rejected: A separate breadcrumb line in the Studio chrome (the spec original default), and deferring US6 entirely.

decisions.decision: Footer row is the WHOLE journey, path-scoped: completed questions + current position + upcoming stages
decisions.why: Author directive. Stages get dots too (reverses Q2 default), visually distinct by size or shape as well as colour so FR-046 non-colour-cue holds. Nothing off the author path is shown, not even greyed out - a dot for a question they will never see misrepresents the length of the journey.
decisions.rejected: Completed-only history row (the spec original), and showing off-path or not-taken-branch questions greyed out.

decisions.decision: Look-ahead reads the flow map existing path projection; row grows when an optional question is reached
decisions.why: dashboard/manifestProjection.ts already computes the projected remaining path with track scoping and resolved forks, so path-scoping, growth on reaching an optional question, and tail re-projection on a branch resolving all fall out of its semantics. FR-049b forbids a second derivation.
decisions.rejected: A footer-local derivation of what comes next - it would drift from the flow map answer, and two surfaces disagreeing about the remaining path is worse than either being wrong.

decisions.decision: Dot timing is hybrid: dots from the decision record, current-position marker from traversal state
decisions.why: Answers are recorded at step completion, so a record-derived marker would be step-granular - and multi-question steps are the longest stretches of the walk, exactly where where-am-I matters most. Traversal state gives per-question position for free.
decisions.rejected: Changing the recording path to commit per question - it moves 053 capture boundary, affecting the diff attached to each entry and the supersession chains, a real regression risk to a shipped surface for an outcome traversal already provides.

decisions.decision: Q1: dot exclusion by construction only, no opt-out flag in v1
decisions.why: A dot exists exactly when the question recorded a decision entry, so notice nodes and acknowledgement screens are excluded with no filter written, while a substantive question that merely has confirm in its id (pb_rtl_direction_confirm, a required routing boolean) correctly keeps its dot. Also removes a Content-team hand-off, since no question is known to need suppressing.
decisions.rejected: A sparse per-question opt-out field (the spec default - would ship unused), and an explicit allow-list (a second source of truth that rots as questions are added).

decisions.decision: Q4 read-only Compare and Q3 revise-and-return default, both confirmed as planned
decisions.why: Read-only makes isolation structural rather than guarded, which is what FR-025 asks an adversarial test to establish. Revise-and-return keeps a one-field correction cheap; continue-from-here is an explicit affordance rather than a prompt on every revision.
decisions.rejected: Sandboxed Compare editing a throwaway copy; revise-and-re-walk as the only model; prompting after every revision.

decisions.decision: Q1 SPLIT: tab-roundtrip stays in Phase 1 Setup; compare-isolation stays too but T004 is rewritten to pin its red-reason
decisions.why: km-testing found spec.md guidance (model on switch-base-exploration/switch-base-rebase) points at the wrong component: those drive editors/panels/BaseResolution.tsx which has base-card-*/base-confirm testids, while the tab picker is components/BaseKeyboardPicker.tsx - a combobox with ZERO data-testid and no confirm button (verified: grep -c data-testid returns 0). A literal port dies on selector-not-found, which is a worthless red and does not satisfy FR-080. T004 now pins an identity-control-absence anchor (TrackOneIdentityPanel.tsx:80,94, removed by T033) plus a dialog-counting harness with BOTH dismiss and accept branches, since a dismiss-only test is a non-signal pre- and post-fix.
decisions.rejected: Leaving T004 at the spec s level of guidance and trusting the implementer to notice the component mismatch.

decisions.decision: Q2 REVERSED: T006 (the D-1 deletion) moves from Phase 2 Foundational into Phase 3 US1, landing in the same wave as T023
decisions.why: km-frontend refuted the blocks-all-stories claim against the code: US2 and US5 do not depend on the deletion at all, and US4 only depends on it for T051 s dot click-through, so it fails the test that defines the Foundational phase. Decisive second finding: landing it in Phase 2 would put the deletion BEFORE T020-T022 rewrite the three suites that encode the old reset contract, opening an unplanned red window on unrelated tests. Also resetOrRestoreSettledRef is not separable from T023 - split across a phase boundary the DEV ordering guard goes SILENTLY INERT (optional param becomes undefined) rather than failing, which is the exact risk research D-9 warns about.
decisions.rejected: Keeping T006 in Foundational on the reading that a jump cannot work on a wizard that forgets its position - true for US3 and US6, but not for US2, US5, or the US4 dot row.

decisions.decision: Q3 REVERSED: FR-041 s stated precedence wins (scaffoldSpec -> identity patch -> baseKeyboard -> null); research D-8 corrected, and T015 widened to converge BOTH shipped draft engines
decisions.why: km-doc found research D-8 examined the wrong function. There are two coexisting draft engines. draftPersistence.ts:477-481 - the engine behind the My keyboards cards, imported at MyKeyboardsList.tsx:51 - already implements FR-041 s order verbatim, comment included (verified directly). draftAutosave.deriveLabel:180-187 is the outlier. So the blast-radius argument that carried the original decision was backwards: conforming deriveLabel renames NOTHING on the cards; its only reader is ResumeDraftBanner.tsx:90, and only when identityResult disagrees with scaffoldSpec, a case with zero test coverage. Spec 047 settles it independently - it describes the label as derived from workingCopy.identity (the identity patch), not survey.identityResult.
decisions.rejected: Keeping the shipped draftAutosave order and treating FR-041 s parenthetical as a loose paraphrase - it was quoting real shipped code all along.

decisions.decision: progressDots derives upcoming stages by walking ctx.manifest forward and asking resolveLocation about each step, rather than importing dashboard/manifestProjection.ts as FR-049b words it
decisions.why: Verified against .dependency-cruiser.cjs: the decisions-layer rule forbids decisions/ -> dashboard/ at severity error, with no type-only exception. manifestProjection is a 1:1 projection of steps/manifest.ts and adds no derived ordering, so reading ctx.manifest reads the same array. FR-049b forbids a SECOND derivation of the projected path; path-scoping, row growth and tail-shrink all fall out of resolveLocation here rather than being re-derived, so the intent holds while the layer rule stays intact.
decisions.rejected: Importing dashboard/manifestProjection.ts as the FR literally says - it is a hard depcruise error; and relaxing the layer rule to permit it, which trades an architectural boundary for a wording match.

plan.summary: Plan + research + data-model + two contract docs written; Constitution Check passes all eight Articles with no violations, one declared Content-team hand-off for the message-id retirement.
plan.key_finding: The reported defect is a one-line deletion: SurveyView mount reset at StudioShell.tsx:452-458 is the ONLY non-explicit surveySessionStore.reset() call site, and both genuine start-over paths already reset explicitly - so FR-002/003/005/007 and defects D-2/D-3/D-4 all fall out of removing it, with no replacement mechanism.

tasks.summary: 74 tasks across 9 phases: Setup (gating red baseline, T001-T005), Foundational (location vocabulary + view-state store + project label, T006-T019), then one phase per story US1/US2/US3/US4/US5/US6 (T020-T065), then Polish (T066-T074). 58 requirements mapped to tasks.
tasks.key_finding: FR-080 inverts the usual order: the two gating E2E specs must be authored and recorded red BEFORE the fix, so they sit in Setup rather than inside their stories. The D-1 deletion sits in Foundational rather than US1 because the spec is explicit that a jump cannot work at all on a wizard that forgets its position - US3, US4, US5 and US6 all depend on it.

FR-001.title: Hold the author's location in a single addressable model, not in component lifetime

FR-002.title: Switching top-level tabs MUST NOT reset or mutate wizard traversal state or any authoring store

FR-003.title: Distinguish starting a new session from navigating within one; reset only on explicit start-over

FR-004.title: Persistence MUST NOT record a position the author did not navigate to

FR-005.title: Navigating into the wizard with a target step set MUST arrive there, with no prior durable-storage read

FR-006.title: No second router, second traversal store, or second notion of the walked path

FR-007.title: Re-entering characters at build-list substage MUST NOT clear the Phase B draft alphabet

FR-008.title: Every wizard entry point lands where it says, covered by a test that fails if a reset reappears

FR-010.title: Support addressing a location finer than a tab: tab, step, question

FR-011.title: A location MUST be expressible in the address bar, shareable, and restorable

FR-012.title: Navigating to a location is a single operation: arrive, or refuse with a stated reason

FR-013.title: Refuse an unreachable location and state which reason applies rather than approximating

FR-014.title: A refused or degraded location lands on the nearest valid ancestor and says so

FR-015.title: The first-visit gate preserves the requested location and honours it on exit

FR-016.title: Browser Back remains correct; the two accepted degrades are not reopened

FR-017.title: Re-derive the history bridge's premise against the preserved-position contract

FR-020.title: The Preview tab is labelled Compare in every locale, taking a new message id

FR-021.title: The Compare tab MUST NOT write to the working copy, survey session, Phase B draft, or decision record

FR-022.title: Selecting a keyboard on Compare MUST NOT instantiate or rebase, and MUST NOT surface a rebase dialog

FR-023.title: The Compare tab exposes no editing controls at all; isolation is structural

FR-024.title: The Compare tab can load, run, and read the source of a keyboard the author is not authoring

FR-025.title: A test asserts the isolation directly via full working-copy state comparison

FR-026.title: The rename is swept across every surface naming this tab; unrelated uses are not renamed

FR-030.title: Each trail entry offers an affordance navigating to its question or stage

FR-031.title: Arriving by deep link shows the currently-recorded answer

FR-032.title: Changing a deep-linked answer records a superseding entry through the existing append-only path

FR-033.title: Changing an answer re-propagates through the existing staleness mechanism

FR-034.title: After a revision the author can both return and continue from here, explicitly

FR-035.title: Entries whose target is unreachable present the reason in place of a link

FR-036.title: The deep-link affordance causes no impact resolution on render

FR-040.title: A narrow footer on tabs where a project exists, from theme tokens, not reducing walk space

FR-041.title: The footer shows the project name via the same precedence the draft layer uses

FR-042.title: The dot row is a whole-journey strip with three classes of mark in journey order

FR-043.title: Each dot is a real focusable control with a localized accessible name

FR-044.title: Hover reveals the label; the same label is available without hovering

FR-045.title: Activating a reached dot uses the same jump mechanism as the trail deep links

FR-046.title: Dots convey class and state by size or shape as well as colour; contrast and focus hold

FR-047.title: Overflow degrades legibly, every mark reachable, current position visible without scrolling

FR-048.title: All footer strings including accessible names and tooltips go through the catalog

FR-049.title: The dot row is scoped to this author's path and grows and shrinks as the path resolves

FR-050.title: Returning to a tab restores section, collapse set, pane split, OSK mode, and scroll position

FR-051.title: View state is session-scoped and is not written into the durable draft in v1

FR-052.title: View state clears on start-over, together with the session it belongs to

FR-053.title: Restoring view state triggers no recompile, re-validation, or authoring side effect

FR-060.title: The footer marks the author's current position with a non-colour cue

FR-061.title: The current-position marker is not a jump target to itself and names the current question

FR-062.title: The footer reads position from the same location model, not the rendered component tree

FR-063.title: Jumping back MUST NOT remove the dots ahead of the landing point

FR-070.title: The 300 ms validation cycle remains the only validation debounce

FR-071.title: The existing durable-draft envelope round-trips unchanged for pre-feature drafts

FR-072.title: Tests encoding the old contract are updated, not deleted; walk helpers updated in the same change

FR-073.title: The message-catalog gates pass with the renamed and added ids

FR-080.title: The two gating specs are written to fail against main first, and that failure is recorded

FR-081.title: E2E stays out of the unit CI lanes; a green run is a deliberate, reported prerequisite

FR-082.title: New E2E steps land in the shared surveyFlow helper rather than copy-pasted per spec

FR-083.title: No spec added by this feature may be committed skipped

concerns.note: src/hooks/useValidator.test.ts failed once under the full `pnpm -r test` run (VALIDATOR_ERROR_FINDING injection case) and passed on its own and on an immediate full re-run. Pre-existing flake, not introduced by this feature, but it can turn a clean gate red intermittently.

FR-060/FR-062 question-level accuracy of the current-position dot holds only right after a trail deep-link arrival (read from peekPendingJump). For ordinary forward walking inside a multi-question step such as characters, no store exposes which question is on screen, so the current dot degrades to stage granularity. Closing this needs a runtime change in the survey runner, outside this feature scope.
